works.abstract: Polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) pollution has emerged as critical environmental and public health concerns due to their potential for bioaccumulation and systemic toxicity. While our previous work demonstrated the trophic transfer of micro- and nanoplastics from insect yellow mealworms (Tenebrio molitor) to mammals, the biological consequences remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the impact of food chain-transferred PS-NPs (FCT-NPs) on the gut-liver axis in a mouse model. We demonstrate that FCT-NPs induce gut microbiota dysbiosis, disrupt metabolic homeostasis, and alter hepatic gene expression in mice. Crucially, we identify the upregulation of Cyp26a1 gene underlying FCT-NPs-induced hepatoxicity, which interferes with retinoic acid metabolism and leads to hypervitaminosis A. By elucidating the molecular link between gut microbial shifts and hepatic dysfunction, this study highlights gut-liver axis as a primary target of FCT-NPs and lays the foundational insights into their broader systemic ecological and physiological consequences.
works.title: Gut microbiota and metabolic disruption induced by food chain-transferred nanoplastics: A mediating role of CYP26A1 in retinoic acid toxicity

works.abstract: Microplastic pollution has emerged as a global environmental and health concern. To elucidate its realistic biological impact, this study established a food chain‑transferred exposure model using polystyrene microplastics, from mealworms to mice. Multimodal analyses of six organs revealed extensive microplastic accumulation and systemic toxicity after exposure. Key molecular interactions involving ADA , APOE , CAT , COL1A1 , FAS , HLA‑DQB1 , ITGB3 , NFE2L2 , NFKBIA , NQO1 , SERPINE1 , TNFRSF1A , VEGFA , CCR2 , and HLA‑DQA1 collectively linked oxidative, immune, fibrotic, and metabolic pathways, forming an integrated cross‑organ toxicity network. These findings demonstrate that food chain‑transferred microplastics induce multi‑layered biological perturbations rather than isolated organ damage, providing new insight into the health hazards of environmental microplastics and highlighting the urgency of long‑term ecological risk assessment.
works.title: Cross-organ multilayered biological perturbations driven by food chain-transferred microplastics: implications for mammalian health effects and risks
